subclass: Single-Vehicle Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (CVRPTW)
reference: Toth, P., & Vigo, D. (2002). The Vehicle Routing Problem. SIAM.
math_formula:
### Mathematical Model
Let N = {0, 1, ..., n} be the depot plus customers, and let C = N \ {0}. Each customer i has demand d_i, service time s_i, and service-start time window [a_i, b_i]. The vehicle has capacity Q. Let c_{i,j} be travel distance/time.

Decision variables:
- x_{i,j} in {0,1}: 1 if the vehicle travels directly from node i to node j.
- t_i: service start time at customer i.
- u_i: cumulative load after serving customer i.

Objective:
minimize sum_{i in N} sum_{j in N, j != i} c_{i,j} x_{i,j}.

Core constraints:
- x_{i,i} = 0 for every node i.
- Each customer has exactly one incoming arc and one outgoing arc.
- Exactly one route leaves the depot and exactly one route returns to the depot.
- If arc (0,j) is used, t_j is at least the depot-to-j travel time.
- If arc (i,j) between customers is used, t_j >= t_i + s_i + c_{i,j}.
- a_i <= t_i <= b_i for every customer i.
- If arc (0,j) is used, u_j is at least d_j.
- If arc (i,j) between customers is used, u_j >= u_i + d_j.
- d_i <= u_i <= Q for every customer i.

The internal generator constructs each instance from a latent feasible route and derives time windows from that route, so the source instance is intentionally feasible.
natural_language_example: A same-day delivery dispatcher has one vehicle starting and ending at a depot. The vehicle must visit each customer exactly once, respect customer service-start time windows, account for service times and travel times, and keep cumulative delivered demand within vehicle capacity. The objective is to minimize total route distance. The generated instances include a depot, customer demands, service times, travel distance matrix, time windows, vehicle capacity, and a latent feasible route used only to guarantee feasibility.
